title: Justice That Is Fair and Measured

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: When people have a dispute, they are to take it to court and the judges will decide the case, acquitting the innocent and condemning the guilty. If the guilty person deserves to be beaten, the judge shall make them lie down and have them flogged in his presence with the number of lashes the crime deserves. - Deut 25:1-2 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God gives instructions for handling disputes justly. Judges were to hear the case, acquit the innocent, and condemn the guilty. And if punishment was due, it was to be carried out in proportion to the crime, "the number of lashes the crime deserves." God's justice is careful and measured. It does not let the guilty go free, nor does it crush them beyond what is fair.

Notice the balance here. God cares that the innocent are cleared, not wrongly punished. He also cares that the guilty are held accountable, but never excessively. Justice under God is neither soft nor cruel. It is precise, fitting the response to the actual wrong done. This protected people from both corruption and brutality.

This reveals the character of our God, who is perfectly just. He never lets true evil go unaddressed, yet He never punishes beyond what is right. We can trust that God's judgments are always fair, never arbitrary or excessive. And how grateful we can be that, though we are truly guilty before Him, Jesus bore the full punishment our sin deserved, so that we can be acquitted, declared innocent, not because justice was ignored, but because it was fully satisfied in Christ (Rom 8:1). God's perfect justice and His mercy meet at the cross. Do you trust that God's justice is always fair, and have you received the acquittal He offers in Jesus?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you trust that God's judgments are always fair?
2. How does Christ satisfying justice for you bring peace?
3. Where do you need to rest in your acquittal in Christ?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You are perfectly just, never excessive, never overlooking wrong. Thank You that in Christ I am acquitted, because justice was fully satisfied. Amen.
